title: Ambedkar and Anup Singh: When the Demon Enters the Temple — 1955
summary: When challenged on why he once said he would burn his own Constitution, Ambedkar electrified the house: 'We built a temple for God to reside; but if a demon enters before God is installed, what choice is there but to tear down the temple?'
keywords: Ambedkar and Anup Singh: When the Demon Enters the Temple — 1955
Dr. B. R. Ambedkar & Dr. Anup Singh
full_text:
In September 1955, the Rajya Sabha was engrossed in a fierce constitutional debate. Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, seated on the opposition benches, was scrutinizing the central government's implementation of social justice safeguards.

Congress member Dr. Anup Singh rose to challenge the Chief Architect of the Constitution:
"Mr. Chairman, Sir! The distinguished Dr. Ambedkar, who earned eternal glory by drafting our Constitution, made an astonishing statement in this very house some time ago. He declared: 'I shall be the first person to burn this Constitution!'
Would a father burn his own child? Will Dr. Ambedkar explain to this nation why he uttered such a shocking threat against the sacred document he himself created?"

A heavy silence descended upon the chamber. Members leaned forward, anticipating an explosive confrontation.

Dr. Ambedkar rose with deliberate majesty. His dark eyes flashed with intellectual fire:
"Mr. Chairman, Sir! I am grateful to my friend Dr. Anup Singh for raising this question. On that earlier occasion, I did not have the time to explain my reasons. Today, I shall provide the explanation through a simple parable."

The house listened in rapt attention.

Ambedkar's deep voice boomed through the hall:
"Friends! Suppose our people labor together to construct a magnificent temple so that God may reside within it and bless the poor.
We build the walls, the pillars, and the sanctum sanctorum. But before we can formally consecrate and install the idol of God, an evil demon slips inside in the dark of night and takes permanent possession of the temple!
What are we to do then? If we lack the strength to drive the demon out, what alternative remains but to demolish the temple itself rather than allow a demon to be worshipped in the name of God?"

Member P. K. Sinha interjected: "Dr. Ambedkar, why destroy the temple? Why not simply destroy the demon?"

Ambedkar fired back with blistering speed:
"Because we do not have the moral courage or the strength to destroy the demon! That is the tragic curse of Indian society!
If those who capture power use this Constitution not to install the God of Equality, Liberty, and Fraternity, but to entrench the demon of caste privilege and oligarchy, then this Constitution ceases to be a sacred temple. It becomes an instrument of oppression. And for the oppressed, burning such an instrument is the only path to self-respect!"

The Rajya Sabha erupted in stunned murmurs and thunderous applause.

Ambedkar's words were a revolutionary declaration: a nation's constitution is not an unalterable religious scripture to be blindly worshipped, but a living instrument whose sacredness depends entirely on whether it delivers justice to the marginalized.
moral: Constitutions and laws are not idols for blind worship; their legitimacy exists solely in their capacity to deliver justice and equality to the weakest citizens.

quiz.question: What parable did Ambedkar use in the Rajya Sabha to explain why he would burn the Constitution if it failed?
options: The parable of a temple captured by a demon before God could be installed
The story of a sinking ship
A fable about an elephant and a mouse
A tale about a broken chariot
quiz.hint: Ambedkar argued that if a constitution designed for equality is captured by oppressive forces, it loses its sacredness.

quiz.question: What did Ambedkar insist was the true purpose of a constitution?
options: To serve as a living instrument to secure justice and equality for the oppressed
To preserve the wealth of the rich
To remain untouched and unchanged forever
quiz.hint: Ambedkar maintained that a constitution's legitimacy lies solely in securing equality and human dignity.
